eyebrow: The T-SQL Development Course · Chapter Nine
subtitle: Lesson 97 · Transactions, Locking, and Isolation Levels

caption: No dirty reads, and no nonrepeatable reads either.

code:
-- READ COMMITTED: shared lock released
--   the instant each statement's read finishes.
-- REPEATABLE READ: shared lock held
--   until the WHOLE transaction ends.
caption: That one difference is what closes the nonrepeatable-read gap.

code:
-- REPEATABLE READ locks rows it has ALREADY read.
-- A brand-new row, inserted after your first query ran,
-- was never locked -- because it didn't exist yet.
caption: Phantom reads are still possible -- Lesson 94's gap, unchanged.

code:
-- Other sessions writing to rows you've read
-- must now wait for as long as YOUR transaction
-- stays open -- not just one statement.
caption: More correctness, less concurrency -- the dial from Lesson 91, in practice.

subtitle: The strictest standard level -- where phantoms finally stop.
